card.title: The Moon was made in a collision

panels.text: The giant-impact hypothesis says the Moon began in a collision. About 4.5 billion years ago, the young Earth was likely hit by a planet about the size of Mars, nicknamed Theia.
Some of the debris thrown out by the impact later gathered together to form the Moon.
That fits a clue: the Moon has a small iron core and is less dense than Earth. Models suggest the impactor's core sank into Earth's, leaving lighter crust and mantle debris to become the Moon.
The idea was first proposed in 1946 by the geologist Reginald Daly. It is still a hypothesis, and questions remain about the best models.

probes.question: According to the giant-impact hypothesis, what hit the early Earth?
True or false: the hypothesis says the Moon formed from debris thrown out by an impact.

claims.claim: About 4.5 billion years ago the young Earth collided with a Mars-sized planet (Theia)
claims.quote: collided with a Mars -sized co-orbital protoplanet likely from the L 4 or L 5 Lagrange points of the Earth's orbit approximately 4.5 billion years ago

claims.claim: Some ejected debris later gathered to form the Moon (also probe 2)
claims.quote: some of the ejected debris from the impact event later re- accreted to form the Moon.

claims.claim: Moon has a small iron core and is less dense than Earth
claims.quote: The Moon has a relatively small iron core , which gives it a much lower density than Earth.

claims.claim: Impactor's core sank into Earth's, leaving lighter debris to become the Moon
claims.quote: Theia's iron core would have sunk into the young Earth's core, and most of Theia's mantle accreted onto Earth's mantle.

claims.claim: Moon formed from lighter crustal and mantle fragments
claims.quote: it would leave the Moon, which was formed from coalesced ejectae of lighter crustal and mantle fragments
